chunks: And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd Al-Anbāri, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever visits the grave of Al-Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā, knowing his rights, is like the one who visits Allāh on His Throne.

key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (specifically for religious devotion, Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on Ashura?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the eschatological significance of visiting Imām al-Ḥusain (a.s.) on ‘Āshūrā, linking the physical act of pilgrimage to a metaphysical encounter with the Divine Presence. The phrase 'knowing his right' (‘ārifan bi-ḥaqqihi) reflects the Shia emphasis on *ma‘rifah* (gnostic recognition) of the Imam’s authority, elevating the visitation from mere ritual to a profound spiritual union. This equivalence to visiting Allah on His Throne highlights the concept of the Imam as the locus of Divine manifestation (*mazhar*) in Shia theology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd Al-Anbāri, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā while knowing his rights are like those who go to the Ziyārah of Allāh on His Throne.
